'''Mikhail Samuilovich Livsic''' ({{Langx|ru|Михаил Самуилович Лившиц}}; 4 July 1917 – 30 March 2007) was a Ukrainian-born Israeli mathematician who specialized in [[functional analysis]].

== Biography ==
Born in Pokotilova, [[Uma District, Ehime|Uman district]] on 4 July 1917, Livsic moved to Odessa with his family when he was four years old.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk/Biographies/Livsic.html|title=Livsic biography|website=www-history.mcs.st-andrews.ac.uk|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref> His father was an associate professor of mathematics who frequented leading Soviet mathematicians in Odessa like [[Nikolai Chebotaryov]], [[Veniamin Kagan|Veniamin Fedorovich Kagan]], [[Mark Krein]] and [[Samuil Shatunovsky|Samuil O. Shatunovsky]].<ref name="bio" />

In 1931 Livsic graduated from school was a close friend of the mathematician Israel Markowitsch Glasman (1916–1968) at the school.<ref name="bio" /> Both were very interested in philosophy and therefore decided to study natural science and mathematics. After graduation, Livsic attended first a school for radio engineers and from 1933 the newly created Departmenr of Physics and Mathematics of the [[Odessa University|Odessa State University]], with Mark Krein, [[Mark Naimark]] and [[Boris Levin|Boris Yakovlevich Lewin]] as teachers. Krein was one of the major figures of the [[Soviet Union|Soviet]] school of [[functional analysis]] and headed a very active school of functional analysis. Lewin was a prominent Soviet mathematician who made significant contributions to [[Complex analysis|function theory]]. Study colleagues of Livsic were the fellow mathematicians A.P. Artyomenko, [[David Milman]], [[Vitold Shmulyan]], M.A. Rutman and V.A. Potapov.<ref>{{Citation|last=Livšic|first=Moshe|date=1997|pages=1–18|publisher=Birkhäuser Basel|language=en|doi=10.1007/978-3-0348-8944-5_1|isbn=978-3-0348-9838-6|title=Topics in Interpolation Theory|chapter=Vladimir Petrovich Potapov as remembered by colleagues, friends and former students}}</ref>

Originally, he worked on the moment problem, at that time the main research area of Krein, and with quasi-analytical functions. Soon after, he worked on the theory of operators, inspired by the work of [[Marshall Harvey Stone|Marshall Stone]], [[John von Neumann]], [[Abraham Plessner]] and [[Naum Akhiezer|Naum Ilyich Akhiezer]] .

Following the evacuation of the [[Odessa State University]] during the Second World War, Livsic received in 1942 in [[Maykop|Maikop]] his Ph.D. on the application of [[Hermitian operators]] theory to the generalised moment problem under supervision of [[Mark Krein]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=https://www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu/id.php?id=74738|title=Mikhail Livshits – The Mathematics Genealogy Project|website=www.genealogy.math.ndsu.nodak.edu|access-date=2018-09-30}}</ref>

In 1945, Livsic passed his [[habilitation]] thesis on generalisations of von Neumann's [[Extensions of symmetric operators|extension theory]] that was evaluated by prominent mathematicians, namely [[Stefan Banach]], [[Israel Gelfand]], [[Mark Naimark]] and Plessner at the [[Steklov Institute of Mathematics]].

Livsic could not return directly to the Odessa State University following the dismantling of Krein's school under the accusation of promoting too many Jewish mathematicians. Livsic himself was considered not being "suited for representing the Ukrainian culture".<ref name="bio" /> He taught until 1957 at the Hydrometeorological Institute in Odessa, then at the Mining Institute of [[Kharkiv]]. In 1962, he joined the department of mathematical physics at the [[National University of Kharkiv|University of Kharkiv]] at the invitation of [[Naum Akhiezer]]. His study focused on the applications of functional analysis to quantum theory.<ref name="list">{{Cite book|title=Topics in operator theory and interpolation: essays dedicated to M.S. Livsic on the occasion of his 70th birthday|date=1988|publisher=Birkhäuser Verlag|isbn=978-0-8176-1988-6|editor-last=Gohberg|editor-first=I.|location=Basel; Boston|pages=17–20|language=en|chapter=List of publication of M. S. Livsic}}</ref> He worked on the physical interpretation of non-self adjoining operators and he developed a theory of open systems which are physical systems which interact with the environment. These research is compiled in two monographs.<ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Rb8-AAAAIAAJ|title=Operators, oscillations, waves (open systems)|last=Livsic|first=Mikhail Samuilovich|date=1973|publisher=American Mathematical Society|isbn=978-0-8218-1584-7|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|title=Operator colligations in Hilbert spaces|last1=Livsics|first1=M. S|last2=Yantsevich|first2=Artem A|date=1979|publisher=V.H. Winston; Halsted Press : John Wiley & Sons|isbn=978-0-470-26541-3|oclc=490092780|language=en}}</ref> After moving to Tbilissi with his family, he started working on a generalisation of the [[Cayley–Hamilton theorem|Cayley-Hamilton theorem]].<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Livsic|first=M. S.|date=1983|title=Cayley-hamilton theorem, vector bundles and divisors of commuting operators|journal=Integral Equations and Operator Theory|language=en|volume=6|issue=1|pages=250–273|doi=10.1007/bf01691898|s2cid=119438138|issn=0378-620X}}</ref>

He moved to Israel in 1978 and settled in [[Beersheba]]. He became a professor at [[Ben-Gurion University of the Negev]] and started to work with [[Naftali Kravitsky]] on a theory of several commuting operators.<ref name="bio">{{Cite book|title=Topics in operator theory and interpolation: essays dedicated to M.S. Livsic on the occasion of his 70th birthday|last1=Dym|first1=H.|last2=Gohberg|first2=I.|last3=Kravitsky|first3=N.|date=1988|publisher=Birkhäuser Verlag|isbn=978-0-8176-1988-6|editor-last=Gohberg|editor-first=I.|location=Basel; Boston|pages=7–16|language=en|chapter=Biography of M. S. Livsic|doi=10.1007/978-3-7643-8734-1_16}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=Q23uCAAAQBAJ&dq=Moshe+Livsic&pg=PR4|title=Theory of Commuting Nonselfadjoint Operators|last1=Livsic|first1=M. S.|last2=Kravitsky|first2=N.|last3=Markus|first3=A. S.|last4=Vinnikov|first4=V.|date=2013-06-29|publisher=Springer Science & Business Media|isbn=9789401585613|language=en}}</ref><ref>{{Cite book|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=r_t6CwAAQBAJ&dq=Livsic+moshe&pg=PA4|title=Commuting Nonselfadjoint Operators in Hilbert Space: Two Independent Studies|last1=Livsic|first1=Moshe S.|last2=Waksman|first2=Leonid L.|date=2006-11-15|publisher=Springer|isbn=978-3-540-47877-5|language=en}}</ref>
